claims.text: The starting feedstock is AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle-size distribution and morphology typical of LPBF.
Approximately 1 wt% nanoscale Y2O3 should be uniformly pre-dispersed into the AlCrFeNiSi powder before LPBF.
Adding approximately 1 wt% nanoscale Y2O3 will mitigate residual thermal stresses in LPBF-built miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
Adding approximately 1 wt% nanoscale Y2O3 will improve the mechanical properties of LPBF-built miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
Adding approximately 1 wt% nanoscale Y2O3 will simplify LPBF processing of miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
A build-plate preheat of approximately 200 °C will aid process stability.
The proposed conditions include vertically built specimens approximately 2 inches tall.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles act as heterogeneous nucleation sites during rapid solidification.
Y2O3-induced heterogeneous nucleation refines the grain size of printed AlCrFeNiSi.
Y2O3-induced heterogeneous nucleation produces a more uniform microstructure.
Dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles help dissipate localized thermal stresses.
Y2O3 nucleation sites reduce thermal gradients during the LPBF melting-solidification cycle.
Reduced thermal gradients diminish residual-stress accumulation and hot cracking.
Y2O3 provides dispersion strengthening that improves yield strength and ductility.
Relative to unmodified AlCrFeNiSi processed under conventional high-thermal-load LPBF conditions, Y2O3-modified components will have lower residual stress.
Relative to the unmodified control, Y2O3-modified components will have fewer processing-induced defects.
Relative to the unmodified control, Y2O3-modified components will have higher yield strength and ductility.

Conventional LPBF of unmodified AlCrFeNiSi is characterized by high thermal gradients, significant residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties caused by microstructural inhomogeneity and processing complexity.

The expected benefits are limited to miniature LPBF components processed under high-energy-input conditions, while applicability to larger components or substantially different thermal regimes is uncertain.
